newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors ask six years jail for ex-minister.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors ask six years jail for ex-minister.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Thursday demanded a six year jail sentence for sacked defence minister Lee Yang-ho, who has admitted taking bribes and leaking military secrets.
On the opening day of his trial, Lee apologised to the court, a prosecution official said.
"I regret deeply and apologise to the public for stirring up trouble," the official quoted Lee as saying.
Lee was fired from the cabinet on October 17 and was arrested later that month.

He was formally indicted last month on charges of accepting 150 million won ($180,000) as his cut of payments to a Korean-American arms dealer from the Daewoo group in connection with a military helicopter deal.
Daewoo says it paid the money as a commission.
Lee was also charged with leaking details to the arms merchant of military plans to buy sophisticated electronics.

Prosecutors also demanded jail terms of two years each for Sok Chin-chol, former president of Daewoo Heavy Industries who now heads the group's car subsidiary in Poland, and Chung Ho-shin, one-time vice president of Daewoo Heavy.

They demanded three years each for Lee Nam-hee and Kang Jong-ho, employees of a company owned by the arms dealer, on charges of extorting 50 million won from Daewoo by threatening to expose the kickbacks.
All the defendants are standing trial together in a Seoul court. They will be sentenced on December 17, the prosecution official said.
The arms dealer showed up in Beijing shortly after the scandal broke but has since vanished.

The scandal embarrassed President Kim Young-sam by holding up to public ridicule his campaign to clean-up South Korean society. Kim's anti-corruption drive has brought to justice his two predecessors, Roh Tae-woo and Chun Doo Hwan.
Opposition parties called for a new government untainted by bribery.
Last month Kim's health minister Lee Sung-ho stepped down amid corruption allegations involving his wife. He was cleared of any wrongdoing but his wife was charged with bribery.
Lee was sacked as part of a sweeping reshuffle of top military brass after the intrusion of a North Korean submarine in September exposed gaping security holes.
